articles.title: ‘Such adept cover stars’: why dogs are taking over fashion in the ‘AI face’ era
articles.summary: Cute, egoless canines offer a break from a world that feels dominated by ‘nepo babies’ and ‘Maga lady aesthetic’ What do Nicole Kidman, a pair of “nepo babies” and a beagle called Sansa Martínez Berlingeri have in common?
body: The September covers of British Vogue and Vogue US have come under intense scrutiny after their recent release, while their canine counterpoint, Dogue, has been almost unanimously celebrated.

Dogue this year features Bad Bunny’s beagle, Lena Dunham’s Mexican hairless Ingrid and her Chinese crested Cornichon, and Millie Bobby Brown’s miniature poodle. The Bad Bunny cover, shot by Eric Rojas in the nostalgia-tinged style of Lady and the Tramp, features four-year-old Sansa. She stares winsomely at the camera, one paw held tenderly by her owner, her tongue wonky and a bowl of spaghetti in front of her.

This contrasts with the reception for British Vogue’s Kidman cover, shot by Venetia Scott, in which the appearance of the Australian-American actor led to discussions online over what some argued was excessive airbrushing. Others questioned whether it was an AI version of the Practical Magic star.

articles.title: Ditch the giant handbag, don’t overdo the botox and 16 other ways to extend your ‘hotspan’
articles.summary: If ‘lifespan’ is the time you’re alive and ‘healthspan’ the years you’re disease-free, then ‘hotspan’ is the period you’re attractive and vibrant. Want to increase yours? Experts share their tips.
body: Forget 12-step skincare routines, red light therapy and injectables – the single most important thing you can do for your skin is wear UV protection. “Not just sun protection, but UV protection, every single day, regardless of weather or season,” says Dr Jennifer Owens, resident aesthetic expert at the Reborne Longevity clinic in London. “Up to 90% of visible skin ageing is caused by UV exposure – nothing else comes close in terms of impact.”

Beware the misguided logo, warns Guardian fashion columnist Jess Cartner-Morley: “Never, ever wear a sweatshirt or, worse, carry a basket with a slogan that includes the words ‘dance’ or ‘love’. Be cautious of words in French. These are the style equivalent of having a ‘Live, laugh, prosecco’ poster in your kitchen. Sorry, but you cannot buy youthful insouciance at M&S.”

articles.title: Are baby products the secret to better skin? 15 toiletries worth trying
articles.summary: With gentler formulas and lower prices, children’s toiletries can work just as well for adults. From nappy rash cream to nourishing bath milk, these are the products that have earned a place in my routine.
body: There may be plenty of worrying headlines about children using adult beauty products from younger and younger ages, but what about the reverse?

I’ve been a beauty editor for more than a decade, but when I had my first child in 2020, I was immediately impressed with the body washes, bath products and moisturisers designed for babies, particularly as someone with eczema and sensitive skin. The products’ gentler, often fragrance-free formulas are easier on my skin, tend to cost less, and result in a less cluttered bathroom, since we can all use the same things. These are the ones I’m still using – on the entire family – five years on.

This was the only nappy cream I ever used on my children as babies, since it seemed to clear up any hint of a rash before it got bad. But it also works miracles when dabbed on my and my son’s eczema flare-ups (calendula is anti-inflammatory). The lanolin ingredient creates a barrier to lock in moisture, and the calendula and chamomile bring down redness quickly and effectively. It leaves a white cast, though, so avoid using it on your face.
points: With gentler formulas and lower prices, children’s toiletries can work just as well for adults.

articles.title: Can’t beat them? Eat them! Ten of the tastiest garden weeds
articles.summary: Edible weeds grow in abundance in our gardens, streets and parks. With a little know-how, you can harvest delicious, nutritious, free greens. Did you know that free food grows in our gardens, streets and parks without being planted by us?
body: We walk past edible weeds without a second thought, yet they’re nutritious and available for much of the year. They return of their own accord every year, either perennially or by seed, making it easy to familiarise yourself with them and learn how to cook.

A number of plants on this list are leafy greens that can be eaten in salad or cooked like spinach. This may feel repetitive (not another spinach substitute!) but is useful when gathering food in or around your garden because you can combine them. This helps if there is a limited quantity of one type, and increases the variety of flavour and nutrients in your diet.

As with any foraging, only pick and eat plants if you are 100% sure of their identity. Avoid those that have been sprayed with pesticides (don’t pick from busy streets – delve deeper into verges, woodland and from gardens you trust) or close to busy roads, where they can absorb pollution.

articles.title: Bridal Perfume: How to Choose the Right Fragrance for Your Wedding Day
articles.summary: What is the best fragrance for a wedding day? Five experts share their best tips for choosing a bridal perfume that will allow you to relive the cherished moment again and again.
body: One thing I would happily add to our “ magical DIY wedding under the stars ” on my dad’s ranch? An entirely new-to-me fragrance to help, a decade later, step directly through a portal to that party. Bluebonnets and bonfire smoke set the mood then, and camping out during Texas wildflower season can’t (yet!) be bottled. If I’d chosen to add Frédéric Malle and perfumer Dominique Ropion’s award-winning Portrait of A Lady eau de parfum to my stroll down the grassy aisle, could I now be transported from the comfort of a sectional with a single spritz? Maybe, according to some experts.

“Scent can be a powerful trigger of certain memories,” says Matthew Robison, assistant professor in the department of psychology at the University of Notre Dame. “We remember events with all their associated features, not only the sensory experience, but also the emotions we were experiencing at the time,” he explains, adding that memory is naturally associative, building connections between these sensory experiences and the people, places, and events surrounding them.

articles.title: Google Will Soon Let You Tell It What Stories You Want to See in Your Discovery Feed
articles.summary: I don't know what the far future of tech looks like, but I know what's in store for the near future: AI. Specifically, AI that responds to natural language prompts. It's already the reality for many platforms, apps, and services: Rather than doing things yourself, you tell the AI what you want…
body: Google announced a handful of changes coming to its self-named app on Friday. Perhaps most notably among the developments is the new ability to "tune" and "tailor" your Discovery feed to your liking—not by giving feedback for specific articles or sources, but by simply telling Google what news you want to see, and what you don't.

If you aren't happy with Gemini's first interpretation of your instruction, you can refine it before refreshing your feed. You can send another prompt (e.g., "can you focus on eco-friendly and sustainable upgrades?") and see how Gemini responds. You can repeat this process until you're happy with the direction Gemini is taking, then hit "Refresh your feed" to see what it came up with. (Of course, you can tap a three-dot menu again to continue changing the experience.) Google says these updates will roll out "in the coming days."
points: I don't know what the far future of tech looks like, but I know what's in store for the near future: AI.
Specifically, AI that responds to natural language prompts.

articles.title: The Best Face Mists Make Tired Skin Look Instantly Refreshed
articles.summary: From Avène, Rhode, Chanel, and more, the best face mists are the key to quenching dry skin. Shop expert-approved ones now.
body: The beauty industry is constantly revealing alleged must-have products to add to your routine, but the best face mists aren’t just marketing—they can actually add major benefits. It’s just about finding the right formula for you.

“Apart from feeling refreshed, face mists formulated with the right ingredients can be beneficial for the skin,” says New York City–based board-certified dermatologist Michelle Henry, MD, citing hyaluronic acid, rose water, aloe vera, and green tea extract as the nourishing ingredients to look out for. “By delivering these humectant ingredients straight to the skin, face mists can promote moisture retention and help the skin barrier reduce trans epidermal water loss.”

Can all skin types benefit from a facial mist? All of our experts say yes; just take a peek at the ingredients to determine which might be suitable for your skin. Whether you’re looking to hydrate, soothe, or protect the skin, read on to discover our edit of the best face mists to shop now.

articles.title: The End of Summer Calls for Coconut Chrome Nails
articles.summary: The latest take on the glazed donut trend is crisp and vibrant.
body: When you think of white nail polish for summer, the possibilities are endless: from coconut milk to vanilla latte, all the way to shades that give your manicure a mermaid-inspired vibe. A simple yet effective way to highlight your tan, to be reimagined through new textures, finishes, and shades transforming a classic into a masterpiece sure to satisfy even the most discerning trend-setters. For summer 2026, the trend to follow is coconut chrome nails, which are created when a bright, crisp white is topped with chrome powder.
You can’t talk about chrome nails—white or otherwise—without mentioning the inventors of the glazed donut nails, Hailey Bieber and her go-to nail artist Zola Ganzorigt.

Coconut chrome is 2026’s update to the long-standing (and still, very popular!) trend. Instead of a nude shade like OPI’s Bubble Bath or Put It In Neutral as the base, try a shade of white. There are so many to choose from, which include crisp and saturated tones as well as softer, warmer shades.
